config.display_name: Lakeview ER Staffing, Access, Quality, and Financial Risk - Genie AI-BI
config.description: Genie space for demo_ward_patient_readmission demo with curated questions and SQL instructions

sample_questions.question_text: If we focus on urban sites only, which operational KPI (arrivals, staffing coverage, waits) best explains spikes in LWBS?
Did average readmission risk increase on surge weekends, and is it higher on days with elevated LWBS and long door-to-provider times?
How did patient satisfaction scores change on weekends vs weekdays, and which sites had the largest drop?
At what hours of day do arrivals and queue lengths peak on weekends, and which sites see the most severe queues?
What is the estimated reimbursement at risk by week in September 2025, and what share occurred on weekends?
How much overtime was logged month-to-date in September 2025 by site and region, and how did it correlate with reimbursement at risk?
Which sites and roles had the largest sick leave rates in September 2025, and were they concentrated on weekends?
Where did nurse coverage gaps occur (coverage_gap_flag = true), and how do they relate to LWBS and wait times?
During the surge weekends (Sep 13–14 and Sep 20–21), how did median triage wait and door-to-provider time change vs weekdays?
Which weekends in September 2025 had the highest LWBS rate, and which sites contributed most?

instructions.title: Notes
instructions.content:
This Genie space helps executives monitor September 2025 ER weekend surges across SummitCare’s six sites, and tie volume spikes to staffing misalignment, access/quality impact, and financial risk.

Data model and table usage:
- Use GOLD tables for fast KPI answers:
  • gold_er_quality_daily: LWBS rate (aka left without being seen), median triage wait (minutes), median door-to-provider (minutes), throughput, satisfaction.
  • gold_er_finance_daily: overtime_hours_sum, cost_per_visit_avg, reimbursement_at_risk_usd, cumulative_reimbursement_at_risk_usd.
  • gold_er_operational_hourly: arrivals per hour, throughput per hour, queue_length_median, door_to_triage_median, door_to_provider_median, effective_staffing_hours, nurse_to_patient_ratio (aka N:P ratio), occupancy_pct.
  • gold_er_staffing_daily: scheduled vs effective hours by role, sick_leave_rate, avg_nurse_to_patient_ratio, coverage_gap_flag (true when N:P exceeds policy threshold).
  • gold_er_readmission_risk_daily: avg_readmission_probability, high_risk_share, realized_readmissions_30d.
  • gold_global_filters_bridge: common filters (date, site, region, unit, is_weekend, role, day_of_week).

Business logic highlights:
- LWBS means “left without being seen”. Access metrics include LWBS, triage wait, and door-to-provider. Weekend surges in Sep-2025 raised arrivals 25–35% and increased waits and LWBS, especially at urban sites.
- Nurse-to-patient ratio (N:P) is used as the coverage proxy; coverage_gap_flag = TRUE indicates effective coverage is below policy thresholds.
- Reimbursement at risk is estimated from LWBS and access breaches and is tracked daily and cumulatively by site.
- Overtime hours increased ~22% MTD; use joins between finance and quality daily to examine whether overtime mitigated access degradation.
- Readmission exposure is monitored via daily averages and realized 30-day readmissions; weekend surges show modest uptick, concentrated in LWBS/long-wait cohorts.

Synonyms and natural language mapping:
- LWBS = left without being seen; LWBS rate = lwbs_rate.
- N:P ratio = nurse-to-patient ratio = nurse_to_patient_ratio (hourly) or avg_nurse_to_patient_ratio (daily staffing).
- Door-to-provider time = door_to_provider_median (hourly) or median_door_to_provider_minutes (daily).
- Triage wait = door_to_triage_median (hourly) or median_triage_wait_minutes (daily).
- Coverage gap = coverage_gap_flag.
- Weekend = is_weekend = TRUE; Weekday = is_weekend = FALSE.

Data quality notes:
- Minor telemetry delays in flow metrics (<0.1%) are smoothed in GOLD hourly.
- Provider start/door-to-provider can be null for LWBS; medians are computed from available records.
- Sick leave flags are derived; nurse weekend sick leave rates are elevated in Sep-2025.

Tips:
- Filter to September 2025 for the event window (2025-09-01..2025-09-30).
- Use site and region filters to compare urban vs suburban vs rural.
- Start with quality and finance daily tables for executive KPIs, then drill into operational hourly for root-cause and specific weekend peaks.

instructions.title: Weekend LWBS and Wait Time Comparison by Site
instructions.content:
-- Compare LWBS (left without being seen) and waits for weekends vs weekdays in Sep-2025
SELECT q.site,
       q.is_weekend,
       ROUND(AVG(q.lwbs_rate), 4) AS avg_lwbs_rate,
       ROUND(AVG(q.median_triage_wait_minutes), 2) AS avg_triage_wait_min,
       ROUND(AVG(q.median_door_to_provider_minutes), 2) AS avg_door_to_provider_min,
       SUM(q.throughput_daily) AS total_throughput
FROM ${catalog}.${schema}.gold_er_quality_daily q
WHERE q.date BETWEEN DATE('2025-09-01') AND DATE('2025-09-30')
GROUP BY q.site, q.is_weekend
ORDER BY q.site, q.is_weekend DESC;

instructions.title: Identify Weekend Coverage Gaps (N:P ratio above policy threshold)
instructions.content:
-- Find sites and dates with coverage gaps (nurse-to-patient ratio above threshold) on Sep weekends
SELECT s.site,
       s.date,
       s.role,
       s.coverage_gap_flag,
       s.avg_nurse_to_patient_ratio AS nurse_to_patient_ratio,
       s.sick_leave_rate
FROM ${catalog}.${schema}.gold_er_staffing_daily s
WHERE s.role = 'Nurse'
  AND s.is_weekend = TRUE
  AND s.date BETWEEN DATE('2025-09-01') AND DATE('2025-09-30')
  AND s.coverage_gap_flag = TRUE
ORDER BY s.site, s.date;

instructions.title: Overtime vs Access Quality (Correlation view)
instructions.content:
-- Examine whether overtime hours align with access improvements
SELECT f.site,
       f.date,
       f.overtime_hours_sum,
       q.lwbs_rate,
       q.median_door_to_provider_minutes
FROM ${catalog}.${schema}.gold_er_finance_daily f
JOIN ${catalog}.${schema}.gold_er_quality_daily q
  ON f.site = q.site AND f.date = q.date AND f.unit = q.unit
WHERE f.date BETWEEN DATE('2025-09-01') AND DATE('2025-09-30')
ORDER BY f.site, f.date;

instructions.title: Reimbursement at Risk by Weekend and Site
instructions.content:
-- Summarize reimbursement at risk by site for weekends in Sep-2025
SELECT f.site,
       SUM(CAST(f.reimbursement_at_risk_usd AS DOUBLE)) AS weekend_reimbursement_at_risk_usd,
       MAX(CAST(f.cumulative_reimbursement_at_risk_usd AS DOUBLE)) AS cumulative_reimbursement_at_risk_usd
FROM ${catalog}.${schema}.gold_er_finance_daily f
WHERE f.is_weekend = TRUE
  AND f.date BETWEEN DATE('2025-09-01') AND DATE('2025-09-30')
GROUP BY f.site
ORDER BY weekend_reimbursement_at_risk_usd DESC;

instructions.title: Weekend Hourly Surge Signature (Arrivals vs N:P)
instructions.content:
-- Show hourly arrivals and nurse-to-patient ratio to visualize surge and coverage
SELECT o.site,
       o.date,
       o.hour_of_day,
       o.arrivals,
       o.queue_length_median,
       ROUND(o.door_to_triage_median,2) AS door_to_triage_median_min,
       ROUND(o.door_to_provider_median,2) AS door_to_provider_median_min,
       ROUND(o.nurse_to_patient_ratio,3) AS nurse_to_patient_ratio
FROM ${catalog}.${schema}.gold_er_operational_hourly o
WHERE o.is_weekend = TRUE
  AND o.date BETWEEN DATE('2025-09-01') AND DATE('2025-09-30')
ORDER BY o.site, o.date, o.hour_of_day;

instructions.title: Readmission Exposure on Surge Weekends
instructions.content:
-- Weekend readmission risk and realized readmissions by site in Sep-2025
SELECT r.site,
       r.is_weekend,
       ROUND(AVG(r.avg_readmission_probability),4) AS avg_readmit_prob,
       ROUND(AVG(CAST(r.high_risk_share AS DOUBLE)),5) AS high_risk_share_avg,
       SUM(r.realized_readmissions_30d) AS readmissions_30d
FROM ${catalog}.${schema}.gold_er_readmission_risk_daily r
WHERE r.date BETWEEN DATE('2025-09-01') AND DATE('2025-09-30')
GROUP BY r.site, r.is_weekend
ORDER BY r.site, r.is_weekend DESC;

instructions.title: Notes
instructions.content:
This Genie space monitors alignment of ER staffing to patient flow and the resulting quality and financial impacts for SummitCare Health Network during September 2025.

Data model and business logic:
- Use gold tables for executive KPIs and NLQ answers:
  - gold_er_quality_daily: LWBS rate, median triage wait, median door-to-provider, throughput, satisfaction; includes is_weekend and day_of_week.
  - gold_er_operational_hourly: Hourly arrivals, throughput, queue length median, waits, effective staffing hours, nurse_to_patient_ratio.
  - gold_er_staffing_daily: Scheduled/effective hours and sick_leave_rate by role (focus on Nurses); coverage_gap_flag indicates nurse-to-patient ratio above policy threshold.
  - gold_er_finance_daily: Overtime hours, cost per visit, reimbursement_at_risk_usd and cumulative.
  - gold_er_readmission_risk_daily: Avg readmission probability, high-risk share, and realized 30-day readmissions by site and weekend flag.
- Weekend surge focus: Fri–Sun spikes starting 2025-09-05, peaking 09-13–09-14 and 09-20–09-21; expect increases in arrivals, waits, LWBS (~+15% relative), and reimbursement at risk.
- Root-cause alignment: Elevated nurse sick leave (doubling to ~6.5% weekends), shift coverage gaps, and HR change logs (09-12 float pool memo; 09-19 on-call expansion) visible via staffing trends.
- Sensitivity: To test “add 2 triage nurses on weekend evenings,” compare urban sites’ hourly nurse_to_patient_ratio and waits (hours 18–23) before vs after the HR changes; expected effect is shorter waits and lower LWBS.

NLQ guardrails and guidance:
- When asked to compare weekends vs weekdays, filter by is_weekend and group by site/date or day_of_week.
- For coverage gaps, use coverage_gap_flag (gold_er_staffing_daily) and nurse_to_patient_ratio (gold_er_operational_hourly). Do not infer causality; describe correlations.
- For readmission impact, use gold_er_readmission_risk_daily; clarify that probabilities are model-derived and observational.
- For finance questions, use reimbursement_at_risk_usd and cumulative_reimbursement_at_risk_usd from gold_er_finance_daily; link patterns to LWBS and wait breaches via quality daily.

Data quality notes:
- Minor telemetry delays (<0.1%) handled in silver flow metrics; daily/ hourly medians already smoothed.
- Some nulls for door-to-provider at hourly granularity; daily medians preferred for executive answers.
- Synthetic data; no PHI. Readmission probabilities are predictive, not causal.

Recommended analysis patterns:
- Aggregate by September 2025 date range and segment by site (Urban vs Suburban vs Rural) and is_weekend.
- Drill from daily KPIs to hourly operational metrics to see evening peak dynamics (18:00–23:00).
- Join staffing daily with quality daily on (site, date) to narrate volume→coverage→quality impacts.

instructions.title: LWBS Rate and Weekend Peaks by Site
instructions.content:
-- Daily LWBS rate and weekend flag
SELECT site, date, is_weekend, visits_total, lwbs_rate, median_triage_wait_minutes, median_door_to_provider_minutes
FROM ${catalog}.${schema}.gold_er_quality_daily
WHERE date BETWEEN DATE('2025-09-01') AND DATE('2025-09-30')
ORDER BY date, site;

instructions.title: Staffing Coverage and Sick Leave (Daily, Nurses)
instructions.content:
-- Nurse coverage and sick leave spikes
SELECT site, date, is_weekend, role, effective_hours, sick_leave_rate, avg_nurse_to_patient_ratio, coverage_gap_flag
FROM ${catalog}.${schema}.gold_er_staffing_daily
WHERE role = 'Nurse' AND date BETWEEN DATE('2025-09-01') AND DATE('2025-09-30')
ORDER BY date, site;

instructions.title: Hourly Arrivals vs Coverage and Waits (Urban Sites)
instructions.content:
-- Hourly operational alignment for surge analysis
SELECT site, date, hour_of_day, is_weekend, arrivals, throughput, queue_length_median, door_to_triage_median AS triage_wait_median, door_to_provider_median, effective_staffing_hours, nurse_to_patient_ratio
FROM ${catalog}.${schema}.gold_er_operational_hourly
WHERE region = 'Urban' AND date BETWEEN DATE('2025-09-01') AND DATE('2025-09-30')
ORDER BY site, date, hour_of_day;

instructions.title: Finance Impact: Overtime and Reimbursement at Risk
instructions.content:
-- Daily finance KPIs with weekend split
SELECT site, date, is_weekend, overtime_hours_sum, cost_per_visit_avg, reimbursement_at_risk_usd, cumulative_reimbursement_at_risk_usd
FROM ${catalog}.${schema}.gold_er_finance_daily
WHERE date BETWEEN DATE('2025-09-01') AND DATE('2025-09-30')
ORDER BY date, site;

instructions.title: Readmission Risk and Realized Readmissions
instructions.content:
-- Daily readmission risk uplift and outcomes
SELECT site, date, is_weekend, avg_readmission_probability, high_risk_share, realized_readmissions_30d
FROM ${catalog}.${schema}.gold_er_readmission_risk_daily
WHERE date BETWEEN DATE('2025-09-01') AND DATE('2025-09-30')
ORDER BY date, site;

instructions.title: Notes
instructions.content:
This Genie space supports executive and operational analysis of SummitCare’s ER weekend surges in Sep-2025: volume → staffing gaps (effective coverage, sick leave, overtime) → access/quality impacts (triage wait, door-to-provider, LWBS) → financial and readmission risk.

Data model (use gold first):
- gold_er_quality_daily: daily LWBS, median waits, throughput, satisfaction by site/date/weekend.
- gold_er_staffing_daily: scheduled vs effective hours, sick leave rate, avg nurse-to-patient ratio, coverage_gap_flag by site/date/role.
- gold_er_operational_hourly: hourly arrivals/throughput/queues/waits and staffing hours for within-day patterns.
- gold_er_finance_daily: overtime and reimbursement-at-risk estimates by site/date/weekend.
- gold_er_readmission_risk_daily: daily predictive readmission risk and realized 30d readmissions.

Join keys: {date, site, unit}. Filter unit='ER'. For staffing-to-quality comparisons, typically use role='Nurse'.

Business logic notes:
- is_weekend is precomputed in gold tables.
- LWBS rate is already computed in gold_er_quality_daily as lwbs_rate.
- coverage_gap_flag indicates days where staffing coverage fell below policy threshold (derived from operational hourly ratios).

Data quality:
- A small amount of missing wait telemetry exists (null medians on rare days/hours). Prefer daily gold aggregates for executive views; use hourly for peak-hour investigation.
- Readmission risk is model-derived (not causal).

instructions.title: Weekend surge & LWBS ranking (Sep-2025)
instructions.content:
-- Rank days in Sep-2025 by LWBS rate, with site contribution
SELECT
  date,
  is_weekend,
  site,
  visits_total,
  lwbs_rate,
  median_triage_wait_minutes,
  median_door_to_provider_minutes
FROM ${catalog}.${schema}.gold_er_quality_daily
WHERE unit = 'ER'
  AND date >= DATE('2025-09-01') AND date < DATE('2025-10-01')
ORDER BY lwbs_rate DESC, visits_total DESC;

instructions.title: Coverage gaps joined to quality outcomes (daily)
instructions.content:
-- Connect staffing coverage gaps to LWBS and waits (Nurse role)
SELECT
  q.date,
  q.site,
  q.region,
  s.sick_leave_rate,
  s.avg_nurse_to_patient_ratio,
  s.coverage_gap_flag,
  q.lwbs_rate,
  q.median_triage_wait_minutes,
  q.median_door_to_provider_minutes
FROM ${catalog}.${schema}.gold_er_quality_daily q
JOIN ${catalog}.${schema}.gold_er_staffing_daily s
  ON q.date = s.date AND q.site = s.site AND q.unit = s.unit
WHERE q.unit = 'ER'
  AND s.role = 'Nurse'
  AND q.date >= DATE('2025-09-01') AND q.date < DATE('2025-10-01')
ORDER BY q.date, q.site;

instructions.title: Hourly peaks on weekends (arrivals, queues, waits)
instructions.content:
-- Identify weekend peak hours by site
SELECT
  site,
  hour_of_day,
  AVG(arrivals)                AS avg_arrivals,
  AVG(queue_length_median)     AS avg_queue_median,
  AVG(door_to_triage_median)   AS avg_triage_wait_mins,
  AVG(door_to_provider_median) AS avg_dtp_mins,
  AVG(effective_staffing_hours) AS avg_effective_staffing_hours
FROM ${catalog}.${schema}.gold_er_operational_hourly
WHERE unit = 'ER'
  AND is_weekend = true
  AND date >= DATE('2025-09-01') AND date < DATE('2025-10-01')
GROUP BY site, hour_of_day
ORDER BY site, avg_queue_median DESC, avg_arrivals DESC;

instructions.title: Finance impact: overtime vs reimbursement at risk (Sep-2025)
instructions.content:
-- Daily finance view with weekend share
SELECT
  date,
  site,
  region,
  is_weekend,
  overtime_hours_sum,
  reimbursement_at_risk_usd,
  cumulative_reimbursement_at_risk_usd
FROM ${catalog}.${schema}.gold_er_finance_daily
WHERE unit = 'ER'
  AND date >= DATE('2025-09-01') AND date < DATE('2025-10-01')
ORDER BY date, site;

instructions.title: Readmission risk vs access metrics (daily, Sep-2025)
instructions.content:
-- Combine readmission risk with access/quality metrics
SELECT
  r.date,
  r.site,
  r.region,
  r.is_weekend,
  r.avg_readmission_probability,
  r.high_risk_share,
  q.lwbs_rate,
  q.median_door_to_provider_minutes
FROM ${catalog}.${schema}.gold_er_readmission_risk_daily r
JOIN ${catalog}.${schema}.gold_er_quality_daily q
  ON r.date = q.date AND r.site = q.site AND r.unit = q.unit
WHERE r.unit = 'ER'
  AND r.date >= DATE('2025-09-01') AND r.date < DATE('2025-10-01')
ORDER BY r.avg_readmission_probability DESC, q.lwbs_rate DESC;
